UKMTO received a report of an incident 70NM southwest of Aden, Yemen. A vessel was approached and hailed by one white skiff, with five persons onboard. This was followed by an exchange of small arms fire. Two additional skiffs were also reported in the vicinity. Update 001 UKMTO have been made aware that only warning shots were fired and no weapons were directed at either vessel. This incident has now been downgraded to suspicious activity. Authorities are continuing to investigate.
UKMTO has received a report of an incident 2NM north of Oman. The crew have been evacuated and safe. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 50NM north of Muscat, Oman. It has been reported over VHF Channel 16 that the vessel has been struck by an unknown projectile above the waterline. Although the engine room was originally reported as on fire it has now been reported that the fire is under control. Update 001: UKMTO has received confirmation that the vessel was attacked by an Uncrewed Surface Vehicle (USV), and that the crew has been evacuated to shore. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 17NM northwest of Mina Saqr, United Arab Emirates. The Company Security Officer reported that the vessel been struck by an unknown projectile causing a fire. The fire has been extinguished and the vessel intends to continue on its voyage. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 35NM west of Sharjah, United Arab Emirates. It has been reported that an unknown projectile has exploded in very close proximity to a vessel. All crew are safe and well. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO received a report of an incident in the Port of Bahrain. The Company Security Officer reported that the vessel had been struck by two unknown projectiles causing a fire. The fire has been extinguished and the vessel remains in port. All members of the ships crew are safe and have evacuated the vessel. Authorities are investigating. Vessels are to remain cautious and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 137NM east of Muscat, Oman. The Master reported a loud explosion in close proximity of the vessel followed by smoke in the water. The vessel and crew are safe. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 7NM east of Fujairah, United Arab Emirates. The Master reported the vessel being struck by an unknown projectile causing damage to the steel plating. There has been no fire or water intake. All crew reported safe. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 10NM east of Fujairah, UAE. The tanker experienced a loud blast and debris from an unknown projectile was found on the deck. The funnel of the tanker sustained minor damage but no major damage has been observed with no environmental implications. All crew are safe and accounted for. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 2NM north of Oman transiting eastbound in the Straits of Hormuz. A container ship has reported being hit by an unknown projectile just above the water line causing a fire in the engine room. Update 001 – The crew have now abandoned the vessel and all crew are accounted for with no reported injuries. No environmental impact has been reported at this time. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 20NM west of Dubai. A container ship has reported witnessing a splash from an unknown projectile in close proximity to the vessel. No damage to the vessel has been reported. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 30NM southeast of MUBARAK AL KABEER, KUWAIT. The Master of a tanker at anchor, reports witnessing and hearing a large explosion on the port side then seeing a small craft leave the vicinity. There is oil in the water coming from a cargo tank which could have some environmental impact, the vessel has taken on water, there are no fires reported and the crew are safe and well. Update 001 05 Mar 26 – UKMTO has received an update that the discharge from the tanker is ballast water. The tanker remains 30NM southeast of MUBARAK AL KABEER, KUWAIT, in IRAQI TTW’s. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 6NM north of Oman in the Straits of Hormuz. A third-party source has reported a tug being hit by unknown projectiles in the Straits of Hormuz. Authorities are investigating.
UKMTO has received a third-party report of an incident 10NM north of Jubail, Saudi Arabia in TTW. The report is being investigated.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 36NM north of Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. The Master reports witnessing a splash and heard a loud bang in close proximity of a bulk carrier. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 25NM northwest of Ra’s al Khaymah, UAE. The Master of a container vessel has reported that the vessel has sustained damage from a suspected but unknown projectile. Extent of the damage is currently unknown but under investigation by the crew. The Master additionally reports that all crew members are safe and accounted for. Update 001: UKMTO has been informed that there is no environmental impact as a result of the incident.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 11NM north of Oman in the Straits of Hormuz. It has been reported that a cargo vessel has been hit by an unknown projectile in the Straits of Hormuz which has resulted in a fire onboard. The vessel has requested assistance and the crew are evacuating the vessel. Update- 001: The CSO has reported that the fire onboard the vessel has been extinguished and there is no environmental impact at this time. Update 002 - 13 Mar 26: The CSO has reported that some of the crew remain unlocated at this time and authorities continue to investigate.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 50NM northwest of Dubai, United Arab Emirates. The Master of a Bulk Carrier has reported their vessel being hit by an unknown projectile. There is no report of any environmental impact. The crew are reported safe and well. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 5NM south of Al Basrah, in Iraq TTW. A third party reported that two tankers have been struck by an unknown projectile. The CSO of one affected vessel confirmed the attack had caused a fire onboard. The CSO reported that the crew have been evacuated and safe. Investigations to identify the second vessel affected continue. 120140UTCMAR26: The CSO of the second tanker involved has confirmed the vessel was struck and the attack has caused a fire onboard. All members of the crew have been evacuated. No environmental impact has been reported at this time.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 35NM north of Jebel Ali, United Arab Emirates. The Master has reported the container ship was struck by unknown projectile causing a small fire onboard. Full damage assessment impaired by darkness. All crew are reported as safe. No environmental impact has been reported at this time. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 23NM east of Fujairah, UAE. A Tanker has reported being struck by an unknown projectile whilst at anchor. Minor structural damage reported. No injuries to crew. No environmental impact reported. Update- 001: The CSO has reported that investigations indicate that the vessel was subjected to falling debris from interceptions in the vicinity of the vessel. The vessel received minor structural damage however all crew are confirmed as safe. UKMTO have re-classified this incident as Suspicious Activity.
UKMTO has received a report of an incident 11NM east of Khawr Fakkan, UAE. It has been reported to UKMTO that a vessel has been hit by an unknown projectile which has resulted in a fire onboard.
UKMTO has received a report of an incident 4NM east of Ras Laffan, Qatar. It has been reported to UKMTO that a vessel has been hit by an unknown projectile. All crew are reported safe and well.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 15NM north of Sharjah, United Arab Emirates. The Master of a Bulk Carrier reported an explosion from an unknown projectile in close proximity to the vessel. All crew are reported safe. Update 001: UKMTO ATTACK Warning 026-26 has been reclassified after review determined the intended target could not be conclusively identified. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 22NM northeast of RAS TANURA Saudi Arabia. The CSO of the Container Vessel reported 2 unknown projectiles splashing in close proximity, each occurring within 1 hour of each other. The crew are reported as safe. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 31NM northwest of Dubai, United Arab Emirates. The Company Security Officer reported an unknown projectile had struck their tanker on the starboard side causing a fire to the vessel. The crew are accounted for and safe. No environmental impact has been reported. Update 001: The CSO has confirmed the fire is extinguished, and there are no environmental implications resulting from the strike. UKMTO are unable to determine the source of the projectile and continue to investigate

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 17NM north of Ras Laffan, Qatar. The Company Security Officer reported the tanker has been hit by unknown projectile on the port side causing damage to the hull above water line. The crew are reported as safe. There is no environmental impact. Authorities are investigating. UPDATE 001: UKMTO can confirm the vessel was struck by two projectiles. One caused a fire which has since been extinguished. The other remains unexploded within the vessels engine room and is being investigated by the relevant authorities. UKMTO are unable to confirm the source of the projectiles and

UKMTO has received a report of an incident in Khor Fakkan Port, United Arab Emirates. The Master reports witnessing multiple splashes from unknown projectiles, in close proximity of his container ship, whilst alongside conducting loading operations.

UKMTO has received a time late report of an incident 25NM south of Kish Island, Iran. The container vessel was struck by an unknown projectile which has caused damage above the waterline. The crew are safe and accounted for. No environmental impact has been reported. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 54NM southwest of Al Hudaydah, Yemen. A sailing vessel was approached by a skiff with approximately 10-12 people on board, 4-5 of whom were armed with automatic weapons. The crew requested that the sailing vessel stopped and when the Master refused they attempted to pull the skiff alongside the sailing vessel to board. The Master deployed a flare and the skiff turned away and departed to the southeast. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident on 07 Apr 26, 112NM southeast of Ras Al Hadd, Oman. The Master of a Bulk Carrier reported to authorities that his vessel was struck by two unidentified projectiles resulting in a fire onboard. A Pakistan Naval vessel rendered assistance and the incident is now reported complete. This UKMTO warning complements JMICC Pakistan Alert 94/26 Ras Al Hadd, Oman

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 20NM northeast of OMAN. The Master of a Tanker reports being approached by 2 IRGC gun boats, no VHF challenge that then fired upon the tanker. Tanker and crew are reported safe. Authorities are investigating. Oman

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 25NM northeast of OMAN. A report of a Container Ship being hit by an unknown projectile which caused damage to some of the containers, no fires or environment impact reported. Authorities are investigating.
UKMTO has received a report of an incident 3NM east of OMAN. The Master of a Cruise ship reported sighting a splash in close proximity of the vessel.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 15NM northeast of OMAN. The Master of a Container Ship reported that the vessel was approached by 1 IRGC gun boat, no VHF challenge that then fired upon the vessel which has caused heavy damage to the bridge. No fires or environmental impact reported. All Crew reported safe.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 8NM west of Iran. A master of an outbound cargo ship reports having been fired upon and is now stopped in the water. Crew are safe and accounted for. There is no reported damage to the vessel. UKMTO is aware of high levels of activity in the SoH area and encourages vessels to report any suspicious activity. Iran

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 83NM southeast of Eyl, Somalia. The Master of a cargo ship was approached by 2 small craft with armed persons onboard. One small craft approached within 600m, warning shots were fired and the suspicious craft returned fire. The suspicious small craft moved away and made clear of the reporting cargo ship. All crew are safe and accounted for.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 45NM northeast of Mareeyo, Somalia. Military Authorities have reported unauthorised persons taking control of the tanker and manoeuvring the vessel 77NM south within Somali territorial waters. The vessels last known position was 0856N 05032E. UKMTO will continue to monitor.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 6NM North East of Garacad, Somalia. It has been reported that unauthorised persons have taken control of a cargo vessel which has been re-directed to within territorial waters. Due to the increased threat of possible PAG activity, vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO while authorities investigate. Garacad, Somalia

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 500NM east of Mogadishu, Somalia. The Master of a tanker was approached by a PAG whilst transiting south through the Indian Ocean. A larger wooden vessel crossed ahead of the tanker at 1nm. The Master then reported that two additional craft approached from the starboard side and closed to within 400 meters. Upon sighting the vessels armed sentries, both small craft and the mothership turned away. Due to the increased threat of possible PAG activity, vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO while authorities investigate.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident within the IRTC, 92NM southwest of Al Mukalla, Yemen. The Master of bulk carrier has reported being approached by a skiff with a black hull carrying seven armed persons.

UKMTO has received a report of a suspicious approach 84NM southwest of Al Mukalla, Yemen. The Master of a bulk carrier has reported being approached to within 500 metres by 1 green hulled skiff which was accompanied by 1 white fishing vessel.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 11NM west of Sirik, Iran. The Master of a northbound bulk carrier has reported being attacked by multiple small craft. All crew reported safe and no environmental impact reported.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 78NM north of Fujairah. United Arab Emirates. A tanker has reported being hit by unknown projectiles. All crew reported safe. No environmental impact reported. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 36NM north of Dubai, United Arab Emirates. The cargo vessel reported a fire in the engine room, the cause of the fire is unknown at this time. All crew are safe and accounted for. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 14NM west of Mina Saqr, United Arab Emirates. UKMTO received information from a third party that a vessel was on fire and requesting vessels in the vicinity to keep a safe distance from them. The cause of the fire has not been verified at this time No environmental impact reported Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident within the Strait of Hormuz. A verified source reported a cargo vessel has been struck by an unknown projectile. Environmental impact is unknown at time of report.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 23NM northeast of DOHA, QATAR. The Master of a Bulk Carrier reports being hit by an unknown projectile. There was a small fire that has been extinguished, there are no casualties. There is no reported environmental impact. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 38NM northeast of Fujairah, United Arab Emirates. The CSO has reported that the vessel has been taken by unauthorised personnel whist at anchor and is now bound for Iranian Territorial Waters. UKMTO continue to investigate.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 98NM north of Socotra. The CSO of a tanker has confirmed that the vessel was approached by a small craft with five persons onboard. The vessels Armed Security Team fired warning shots at the small craft which forced them to alter course. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident within the IRTC 200NM west of Socotra. The Master of a products tanker has reported that the vessel was approached by a small craft with 5 persons onboard, closest point of approach 100m. The vessel’s Armed Security Team were deployed and the small craft altered course away from the reporting vessel.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 60NM east of Muscat, Oman. The Master of a Tanker reports of an external explosion, Port side aft close to the waterline. The crew and vessel are safe, although the Master reports some bunker fuel has discharged into the sea. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 40NM southeast of Umm Qasr, Iraq. A Cargo Vessel was transiting in the Arabian Gulf when it experienced a large explosion following potential impact from an unknown projectile on the starboard side. UKMTO is unaware of any environmental impact at this time. Update 001: UKMTO has been informed of a second impact to the Cargo Vessel, resulting in a fire which has since been extinguished. No report of injuries to crew.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 15NM northeast of Masirah, Oman. A tanker has experienced a fire onboard resulting in the evacuation of crew. Omani and Indian Authorities are coordinating the response. There are no reports of environmental impact at present.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 20NM northeast of Sohar, Oman. Local authorities have reported a tanker has experienced a fire in their engine room and are on the scene assisting with the evacuation of the crew. The vessel is reporting 1 casualty and 2 crew members missing. No environment impact reported. Authorities continue investigating. Sohar, Oman

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 21NM northeast of Sohar, Oman. Local authorities have reported a tanker has experienced a fire in the engine room. No environmental impact has been reported. Authorities continue to investigate.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 6NM east of Oman. It is reported a Tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in the Port Bow. The Crew are reported safe and there is no reported environmental impact. The tanker is continuing to its next Port of call. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 14NM south off the coast of Yemen. A container vessel has reported being approached by a small skiff. The crew of the small skiff opened fire on the vessel and attempted to board. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 111NM southeast of Aden, Yemen. A tanker has reported being approached by a small skiff with 4 crew. The crew of the skiff were armed and opened fire on the vessel with an RPG. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 105NM northeast of Aden, Yemen. A vessel has been approached to within 4 meters and fired upon by 2 skiffs with an unknown number of armed persons on board. The vessel has deployed security team and returned fire. The suspect skiffs have now disengaged and are in excess 4NM of the vessel. The crew are safe.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 50NM southeast of Al-Shihr, Yemen. The Master of a product tanker reported being approached by a skiff carrying five armed persons who appeared to be attempting to board the vessel. In response, the vessel conducted evasive manoeuvres and altered course away from the skiff. Vessel is now proceeding to its next port of call. The vessel and crew are reported safe. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 7.5NM southeast of Dahit, Oman. A cargo vessel has been hit on the starboard side by an unknown projectile, causing damage to the bridge. Master has reported no casualties and no environmental impact. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident within the Strait of Hormuz. The Master of Tanker has reported being struck by an unidentified projectile. The vessel sustained damage to their bridge; all crew are reported safe. No environmental damage reported at present.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 76NM south of BALHAF, YEMEN. UPDATE 001 – UKMTO have been informed that the suspicious small craft has now departed from the vessel but remains active in the area and could possibly be a risk to other vessels. CSO reports the vessel has minor damage on the bridge and confirms it’s one suspicious small craft with 4 POB, armed with RPG. UPDATE 002 – UKMTO Warning 077_26 has been reclassified as an ILLEGAL BOARDING. The Master has further reported that the unauthorised personnel caused damage to the bridge and several adjacent compartments. The crew remain secure in the citadel and are reported safe

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 85NM south of Balhaf, Yemen. The Master of a tanker had reported a small craft approached the vessel on the port quarter at 2NM. The small craft was described as having a low freeboard and orange interior with 4 POB. The small craft has now left the vicinity proceeding south. The crew are reported as safe and the vessel is continuing on its voyage. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 30NM southwest of Al Hudaydah, Yemen. A cargo vessel has triggered a distress alert stating that they are under attack by unknown armed assailants. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 8NM east of Limah, Oman. A tanker has reported being hit by an unknown projectile on the port side causing a fire, whilst travelling southbound. No casualties or environmental impact reported. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident involving a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile and is believed to have structural damage. No casualties or environmental impact reported.

UKMTO has received a report of a further incident involving a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The tanker was struck by an unknown Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) and has sustained minor structural damage. No casualties or environmental impact reported, and vessel is continuing to its next port of call.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 9NM east of Oman. Military authorities have reported that a container ship has sustained damage to the rear of the vessel which has caused a fire onboard. UPDATE 001: UKMTO has been informed by military authorities and the CSO of the vessel that the crew have abandoned the vessel and are currently embarked in a lifeboat. UPDATE 002: UKMTO has spoken to the CSO of the container ship who confirms that the crew has been rescued by local authorities. Authorities continue to investigate.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 50NM south of Aden, Yemen. A tanker travelling east in the IRTC has reported being approached by 6 small boats approaching from the starboard side. One small boat has closed to 5 cables and the AST on board the tanker has fired warning shots. The other 5 small boats have remained at 1NM. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 40NM northeast of Qalhat, Oman. The Master of a Tanker reports being hit by an unknown projectile on the starboard side engine room. All crew are safe and accounted for with no environmental impact reported.
UKMTO has received a report of an incident 13NM southeast of Limah, Oman. A tanker has reported being hit by a missile while transiting outbound on the southern route. Authorities are investigating.
UKMTO has received a report of an incident 13NM southeast of Limah, Oman. A tanker has reported being hit by a missile while transiting outbound on the southern route. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 19NM east of Khasab, Oman. A tanker has reported being hit by an unknown projectile causing minor structural damage to the port side. All crew are safe and accounted for, no environmental impact has been reported and the vessel is continuing to its next port of call. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 65NM south of Al Mukalla, Yemen. Military authorities have reported that the vessel was boarded by unauthorised personnel whilst transiting east in the Gulf of Aden. UPDATE 001 – Military authorities have reported to UKMTO that the vessel involved has been manoeuvred into Somalian territorial waters. UKMTO has re-classified this incident as Hijack Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 8NM northwest of Kumzar, Oman. UKMTO have received information from military authorities that a vessel is on fire. The cause of the fire has not been verified as this time. Update – 001 UKMTO has reclassified as an Attack. The CSO has confirmed the vessel was struck by an unknown projectile. The crew safely abandoned the vessel and have been recovered by a tug boat. The fire has not been extinguished and the vessel is currently adrift. There is no reported environmental impact.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 17NM east of Dibba, United Arab Emirates. The Master of a vessel reports being struck by an unknown projectile causing damage to the steering gear. All the crew are reported as safe. There is no environmental impact. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 8NM northeast of LIMAH, OMAN UKMTO has received multiple reports that a tanker is reporting over VHF Channel 16 that it has been struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. UPDATE 001: The CSO of the tanker has reported to UKMTO that the crew have abandoned the vessel and are currently embarked in a lifeboat. No environmental impact has been reported. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 70NM southwest of AL SHUQAIQ, Saudi Arabia. The Master of a tanker reports being struck by an unknown projectile which has caused a fire onboard that the crew are currently fighting. There are no reported casualties and no environmental impact.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident in the southern Red Sea. It has been reported to UKMTO that a tanker witnessed a splash from an unknown projectile in close proximity to the vessel. Reports confirm that the vessel and crew are safe. Environmental impact is unconfirmed at present.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 11NM northeast off Lima, Oman. The CSO of a tanker reports the vessel has been struck by an unknown projectile which has caused damage to the engine room. The tanker is not under command and the regional Coast Guard have been informed. There are no reported casualties or environmental impact.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 21NM northeast of Khasab, Oman. The Master of a tanker reports seeing a large splash and explosion in close proximity to the vessel. No damage to the vessel has been reported at this time.
UKMTO has received a report of an incident 20NM northeast of Al Khasab, Oman. A cargo vessel has broadcasted on VHF 16 that they have been hit by an unknown projectile. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a time-late report of an incident 9NM southwest of Al Mukha, Yemen. The CSO of the vessel has reported that the vessel was attacked by an Uncrewed Surface Vessel which caused a fire onboard. The crew have been rescued by local authorities and are safe and well. The vessel has been reported as sunk.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 95NM southeast of Aden, Yemen. The Master of a tanker reported hearing a loud explosion in close proximity to the vessel. All crew accounted for and safe. There is no environmental impact reported. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a time late report of an incident 9NM southeast of Kumzar, Oman. The Master of a tanker has reported hearing two explosions whilst transiting in the Strait of Hormuz. The report confirms that crew and vessel are safe. No environmental damage has been reported.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 18NM east of Khasab, Oman. A verified source has reported that a vessel was struck by an unknown projectile which caused a fire that has been extinguished. There is no reported environmental impact. The vessel and crew are reported as safe.

UKMTO has been informed of an incident off the coast of Al Mokha, Yemen. It has been reported that a cargo vessel in the Southern Red Sea has been hit by an unknown projectile resulting in casualties. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. UKMTO has received reports from Military Authorities that a tanker was struck by a Uncrewed Ariel Vehicle (UAV) whilst conducting an outbound transit of the Strait of Hormuz. The vessel was subject to minor damage, crew are reported as safe and accounted for and no environmental impact has been reported.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. UKMTO has received reports from Military Authorities that a tanker was struck by a Uncrewed Ariel Vehicle (UAV) whilst conducting an outbound transit of the Strait of Hormuz. The vessel was subject to minor damage, crew are reported as safe and accounted for and no environmental impact has been reported.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz UKMTO has received a verified report of a Bulk carrier being struck by an unknown projectile which has hit the hull. The crew are reported safe, no damage assessment has been reported and environmental impact is unknown at present.
UKMTO has received a report of an incident 4NM south of MAREEYO SOMALIA. The CSO of a cargo vessel reports being boarded by 8 armed unauthorised persons who have taken control of the vessel.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. The Company Security Officer has reported that the vessel was struck by an unknown projectile while conducting an outbound transit of the Strait of Hormuz. The impact caused damage to the engine room and resulted in a crew casualty. The remaining crew are currently being assisted by the Omani Coast Guard. At present, no environmental impact has been reported. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a time late report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. A third party has reported that a bulk carrier was struck by an unknown projectile whilst conducting a transit of the Strait of Hormuz. The impact caused damage to the starboard side of the vessel and resulted in a crew casualty. There is no report of an environmental impact.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 40NM southeast of Al Mukha, Yemen. Local Authorities report a cargo ship being struck by multiple unknown projectiles. The cargo vessel was unmanned at the time of the incident; however, the damage has resulted in a complete constructive loss. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 136NM east of Al Mukalla, Yemen. A tanker has broadcast a distress call on VHF 16 that they have been approached by an unauthorised vessel whilst travelling west in the Gulf of Aden. Update 001 – UKMTO have received confirmation that the tanker has been boarded by six armed persons who are now in control of the vessel and redirecting to Somalia. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 63NM west of Yanbu, Saudi Arabia. The Company Security Officer reported a tanker has been struck by unknown projectile causing a fire to the vessel on the main deck. All crew are safe and accounted for and no environmental impact has been reported.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 9NM northeast of Ash Shishah, Oman. The Master of an oil tanker reports the vessel has been struck by an unknown projectile causing damage to the engine room and disabling the vessel. Crew are reported safe. Environmental impact is unknown at time of report.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. Local authorities have reported a tanker has been hit by an unknown projectile causing fire to the vessel which has since been extinguished. All crew are reported as safe and accounted for and there has been no report of environmental impact. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a time-late report of an incident 12NM north of Khasab, Oman. A tanker has been struck by an unknown projectile whilst transiting inbound in the Strait of Hormuz. No casualties or environmental impact are reported at this time. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a report of an incident 17NM east of Khasab, Oman. A tanker has reported being struck by 3 unknown projectiles whilst completing an outbound transit of the Strait of Hormuz. No casualties or environmental impact has been reported. Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO has received a time-late report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. UKMTO has received a verified report that a tanker was involved in a security incident resulting in two casualties. There is no report of environmental impact at this time. Update 001: UKMTO has received confirmation that the two casualties reported in this incident have now been confirmed as fatalities. Authorities are investigating.

Actor / Attribution: Attributed in reporting to Iranian strike activity
Description: Two drones targeted the commercial port; one struck worker accommodation and debris from the second landed near fuel tanks.
Operational Impact: Localized impact; port security response activated
Trade Impact: Direct attack on a commercial port; important benchmark for port resilience and fuel-storage exposure.
Notes: Operator / authority: Port of Duqm / Oman authorities; Status: Confirmed by Oman News Agency

Description: Smoke and fire were reported from the Zayed Port area following Iranian retaliatory strikes.
Operational Impact: Operational disruption reported in wider UAE port response
Trade Impact: Shows conflict spillover directly into urban port infrastructure.
Notes: Operator / authority: Abu Dhabi / port authorities; Status: Confirmed visual reporting; detailed damage not fully public

Description: Missile or drone debris sparked a fire at Jebel Ali Port; smoke was visible over the terminal area.
Operational Impact: DP World paused activities temporarily during the immediate response
Trade Impact: Major global transshipment hub; short disruption has regional supply-chain significance.
Notes: Operator / authority: DP World / Dubai authorities; Status: Confirmed by Dubai/Reuters reporting

Actor / Attribution: Incoming Iranian drone intercepted; debris impact
Description: Debris from an intercepted drone caused a fire at Fujairah; one person was lightly injured and some oil-loading operations were suspended.
Operational Impact: Some oil-loading operations suspended; loadings resumed the next day
Trade Impact: Critical because Fujairah sits outside Hormuz and functions as an energy bypass hub.
Notes: Operator / authority: Fujairah authorities / ADNOC-linked infrastructure; Status: Confirmed; operations subsequently resumed

Actor / Attribution: Likely Iranian strike; local authorities confirmed drone impact
Description: Two drones targeted Salalah Port, injuring one worker and damaging a container crane.
Operational Impact: Port evacuated and operations temporarily suspended; roughly 48-hour estimate reported
Trade Impact: Notable because it extends conflict risk to a major Indian Ocean transshipment port outside Hormuz.
Notes: Operator / authority: Port of Salalah / APM Terminals; Status: Assessed / investigated

Actor / Attribution: Drone strike confirmed by Egyptian cabinet; attacker unclaimed
Description: A drone hit a gas vessel at Damietta and fire spread to a second gas vessel.
Operational Impact: Emergency response; energy-import infrastructure disrupted / assessed
Trade Impact: Direct attack on LNG/FSRU infrastructure broadens port conflict risk beyond Gulf ports.
Notes: Operator / authority: Egyptian authorities / vessel owners; Status: Investigation ongoing

Description: Russian strikes damaged port export infrastructure in the Odesa region and contributed to disruption of export routes.
Operational Impact: Export facilities damaged; wider seaport operations heavily constrained
Trade Impact: Important for grain, Danube rerouting and Black Sea maritime-risk assessment.
Notes: Operator / authority: Ukrainian port authorities; Status: Confirmed by Ukrainian officials; conflict ongoing

Subtype: Drone strike on port and vessels
Location: Port of Izmail / Odesa maritime corridor
Subject Name: Two foreign civilian vessels / port logistics
Description: Russian drones hit Izmail port, damaging port infrastructure and foreign civilian vessels including a Panama-flagged vessel.
Operational Impact: Port operations reportedly remained stable despite damage
Trade Impact: Illustrates direct merchant-vessel exposure inside a functioning wartime export port.
Notes: Operator / authority: Ukrainian authorities; Status: Confirmed by Ukrainian officials

Actor / Attribution: Maintenance-related incident; sabotage not indicated initially
Description: Explosion at a petroleum product storage facility during maintenance killed one and injured six.
Operational Impact: Localized facility impact; major port systems remained operational
Trade Impact: Demonstrates maintenance and hazardous-storage risk inside a major energy port.
Notes: Operator / authority: Gunvor / Rotterdam authorities; Status: Authorities investigating

Subject Name: Wind Orca; BG Orange; 750-tonne gantry crane
Actor / Attribution: Under investigation by police, MAIB and harbour authority
Description: Wind Orca collided with berthed container ship BG Orange and then a quayside crane, causing the crane to collapse.
Operational Impact: Recovery zone established; local operational disruption and cleanup
Trade Impact: Strong combined case: collision + crane loss + cargo/environmental release + operational disruption.
Notes: Operator / authority: Port of Tyne; Status: Investigation ongoing

Actor / Attribution: Load shift / lifting imbalance reported; formal cause under investigation
Description: During a heavy-lift operation, a mobile crane overturned toward the vessel and a fire broke out.
Operational Impact: Berth area secured; investigation and crane recovery required
Trade Impact: Useful port-safety case for heavy-lift procedures, crane stability and berth exclusion zones.
Notes: Operator / authority: Mumbai Port Authority; Status: Safety investigation opened

Actor / Attribution: Cause not stated publicly in Coast Guard release
Description: A crane fell into the Cooper River near Pier G, creating a submerged navigation hazard.
Outcome / Damage: Potential fuel pollution controlled with boom
Operational Impact: 100-yard safety zone; shipping later resumed around hazard
Trade Impact: Demonstrates how shoreside equipment failure can become a channel/navigation incident.
Notes: Operator / authority: US Coast Guard / port stakeholders; Status: Salvage completed 30 Jul; safety zone rescinded

Actor / Attribution: Preliminary indication of steering-control loss aboard BLACK RHINO
Description: Outbound SEA HONOR collided with inbound BLACK RHINO near buoy 20; BLACK RHINO was intentionally grounded after damage.
Operational Impact: Navigation channel temporarily obstructed then reopened
Trade Impact: Direct example of channel blockage risk and emergency grounding to restore access.
Notes: Operator / authority: Port Authority of Douala; Status: Technical investigation ongoing

Description: Containership MAERSK VALPARAISO contacted tanker LADY MARTINA during manoeuvring; both vessels subsequently grounded.
Trade Impact: Combines container-port access, collision, injury, grounding and pollution exposure.
Notes: Operator / authority: Nigerian maritime authorities; Status: Reported casualty / authorities responded

Actor / Attribution: Possible steering gear problem plus strong tidal conditions
Description: Container vessel lost control while navigating the Hooghly, struck the riverbank and grounded.
Operational Impact: Temporary vessel immobilization; refloated at high tide with tug assistance
Trade Impact: Good access-channel case for pilotage, steering reliability and tidal constraints.
Notes: Operator / authority: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port / vessel interests; Status: Cause not yet officially determined

Description: Research vessel Atlantis grounded in Great Harbor Channel at the entrance to Woods Hole and freed itself after about 12 minutes.
Operational Impact: Short-lived channel casualty; vessel moored after refloating
Trade Impact: Includes quantified damage estimate and formal U.S. major marine casualty status.
Notes: Operator / authority: USCG / NTSB / Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution; Status: USCG lead; NTSB major marine casualty investigation ongoing

Actor / Attribution: Water ingress; detailed cause not public
Description: Container vessel took on water and sank about 6 km off Batam; all nine crew were rescued.
Outcome / Damage: No oil pollution reported; potential drifting-container hazard
Operational Impact: Straits traffic unaffected; navigational warnings issued
Trade Impact: Relevant to Singapore/Batam approaches and secondary hazards from floating containers.
Notes: Operator / authority: Indonesian authorities / MPA Singapore / Samudera Shipping; Status: Monitoring / cargo recovery

Location: South of Aleutian Islands / Long Beach-bound
Description: OOCL Sunflower lost dozens of containers overboard while en route to Long Beach; USCG prepared for vessel arrival and cargo assessment.
Outcome / Damage: Potential floating-container hazard; no discharge observed; 32
Operational Impact: Long Beach authorities prepared for arrival inspection; no port closure
Trade Impact: Although offshore, this is directly relevant to container-loss tracking and destination-port response.
Notes: Operator / authority: USCG / NOAA / vessel interests; Status: NOAA/USCG response

Description: Panama-flagged cargo ship Ocean Winner sank off eastern India while carrying iron ore; search and rescue operations followed.
Operational Impact: No direct port closure reported; casualty affected regional voyage
Trade Impact: Port-linked bulk-shipping casualty; useful for route-level risk even though not inside harbour limits.
Notes: Operator / authority: Indian Coast Guard; Status: Search and rescue / investigation

Description: CMA CGM PETRA suffered a cargo-hold fire in the Strait of Malacca; salvors were engaged and the ship remained off Penang.
Operational Impact: Missed scheduled port call; salvage operations ongoing
Trade Impact: Relevant to Malacca/port-call disruption and salvage capacity.
Notes: Operator / authority: CMA CGM / salvors; Status: Fire contained; salvage continuing

Description: Ro-ro passenger ferry contacted a jetty at Holyhead, puncturing the hull and causing engine-room flooding.
Operational Impact: Port-side vessel casualty; detailed disruption assessed by MAIB
Trade Impact: Early-2026 port allision; useful benchmark for berth-contact and flooding risk.
Notes: Operator / authority: Stena Line / Holyhead Port; Status: Completed preliminary assessment

Description: A worker aboard M/V Bruce died after being struck by a large metal beam while the vessel was in Mackay Harbour.
Operational Impact: Localized investigation; no broad port shutdown reported
Trade Impact: Captures occupational safety as a distinct port-incident category.
Notes: Operator / authority: AMSA / North Queensland Bulk Ports; Status: AMSA / coroner process

Description: While the vessel was loading palm kernel shells at berth, the watch helmsman discovered two perpetrators rummaging through the spare parts room in the engine room. The watch helmsman immediately made an emergency call to the ship. The perpetrators fled towards the wheelhouse and jumped overboard from the stern deck upon being noticed. They escaped via a small boat waiting nearby. The crew then conducted a search on board. Some spare parts of the generator were stolen. The crew were not injured. The incident was reported to Polairud Marine Police. The Marine Police carried out information gathering on the ship.

Location: Southwest of Vung Tau Light house, Anchorage H13, Vietnam
Description: At Anchor While at anchor, at least one perpetrator boarded the ship through freeboard on port bow and went to the paint store at forecastle. A thorough search was conducted on board. 75 cans of paints and a set of cables for welding machines were stolen. The crew were not injured. The incident was reported to the local agent and Vung Tau Border Defence Force.

While berthed, the vessel’s shore security watchman and duty crew detected three to four perpetrators near the port- side midship store. The alarm was immediately raised, alerting the crew and security personnel. Upon activation of the ship’s alarm, the perpetrators escaped. A search was conducted and ship stores, including an emergency hydraulic hand pump, hydraulic blowers and spare PV valves, were stolen from the midship store. Investigation revealed the perpetrators gained access to the vessel from the seaside using hooks and ropes, and subsequently forced entry into the locked midship store. The crew was not injured. The Bangladesh Coast Guard (BCG) subsequently boarded the vessel to conduct further investigation.

At Anchor While anchored, two perpetrators wearing T-shirts and shorts boarded the ship from a small boat using a rope and hook via the poop deck port quarter. The alarm was raised and the perpetrators escaped with stolen engine store spares. The crew was not injured.

While the vessel was transiting the Malacca Strait prior to its arrival in Singapore, the third Engineer discovered that the spare store had been disturbed and immediately reported the incident to the Chief Engineer. A subsequent inventory check confirmed that two turbocharger service kits, two main bearing metal assemblies, one crankpin bearing metal, and one piston ring set were missing. All crew members were accounted for and safe. The incident was reported to the flag State.

At Anchor While anchored, during routine safety rounds, the duty AB discovered that perpetrators boarded the vessel. The crew conducted a thorough search of the vessel. However, no perpetrators were found onboard. Subsequent onboard checks revealed that several items were stolen from the bosun store, including a brass bell, electrical wires and cables, butterfly nuts, stools, a chain locker sounding cap, a sounding pipe, and a hydraulic oil refilling cap. All crew members were safe and accounted for. The Master reported the incident through the local agent to the local Port Authority.

Location: Charlie Anchorage, Chittagong Port Area, Bangladesh
Description: While underway, a group of perpetrators boarded the vessel and stole ship stores. As this was a vessel to be scrapped, there was no security staff or watchmen onboard. The ship's local agent informed BCG and Chittagong Port Authority. BCG sent a boarding party to the vessel and conducted an investigation onboard. BCG and River Police subsequently recovered and handed over the stolen items to concern authority and shipping agent.

Location: Approximately 9.7 nm off Pulau Iyu Kecil (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS)
Description: While underway, five perpetrators armed with a knife and a in the engine room. Ship's gun-like object were sighted general alarm was activated, deck lights switched on and all crew mustered. A search was conducted with no further sighting of the perpetrators onboard. All crew were accounted for and were safe. Some engine spares were stolen. The incident was reported to Singapore Vessel Traffic Information System (VTIS). Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch carried out to warn vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the Singapore Strait (SS). Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN) and Singapore Police Coast Guard (SPCG) were notified of the incident. SPCG boarded the vessel and conducted a security search. No perpetrators were found on board. Information was shared with the Indonesian authorities.

At Anchor While anchored, the duty officer onboard noticed several small boats near the forward of the vessel and notified the bosun to check. After several minutes, on not receiving any response from the bosun, the duty officer raised the alarm. Crew mustered and proceeded to the forecastle where they saw the bosun tied up. Seven perpetrators carrying knives were also seen escaping from the forecastle store. On investigating, ship properties were reported as stolen. The incident was reported to Belawan VTS, Coast Guard and the local agent.
While underway, the barge was boarded by three perpetrators. Four lashing wires, eight turn buckles, one solar light and 10 shovels were stolen. The crew on the tug boat were not injured.

Location: Manila International Container Terminal (MICT) Anchorage, Philippines
Description: anchored, four perpetrators armed with knives/bladed weapons boarded the vessel by climbing a rope attached to the forecastle area. Upon boarding, the perpetrators proceeded to the bosun store and forcibly opened the door. After the incident was discovered, the crew immediately secured the area and activated the alarm. Some ship property/stores were stolen. The incident was reported to Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) Manila and Coast Guard Station (CGS) Manila. Upon receiving the report, Coast Guard Sub-Station (CGSS) North Harbor and CGS Manila personnel, together with Investigation Detection Unit (IDU) personnel carried out investigation.

Location: Approximately 3.2 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, four perpetrators were sighted in the engine room. One of the perpetrators carried a gun-like object and three perpetrators were unarmed. The ship’s general alarm was activated, deck lights switched on and the crew was mustered. A search was conducted, with no further sighting of the perpetrators onboard. All crew members were accounted for and safe, with no injuries reported. Some further assistance was engine spares were missing. No required. The incident was reported to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was carried out to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN and SPCG were notified of the incident. Information was shared with the Indonesian authorities. Upon arrival at Eastern Holding A Anchorage (AEHA), SPCG boarded the vessel and conducted a search onboard, with no perpetrators found.

Location: Approximately 1.9 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, two unarmed perpetrators were sighted on deck by crew. The ship’s general alarm was activated, and all crew members were mustered and accounted for. Safety broadcast on anti- piracy watch was carried out to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN and SPCG were notified of the incident. Location: Approximately 2.3 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, three perpetrators armed with knives and gun-like objects were sighted in the engine room. The ship's general alarm was activated and the crew mustered. At Anchor While at anchor, four perpetrators armed with guns and the ship knives were sighted onboard. Upon discovery, immediately reported to VTMS Corregidor and CGS Manila. The perpetrators disembarked via an unidentified motor banca. In response, CGS Manila immediately informed CGSS North Harbor to establish communication with the subject vessel. Despite several attempts, the station failed to get in touch with the vessel or the local agent for the exact location or other details pertaining to the perpetrators’ identity.

At Anchor While at anchor, six perpetrators boarded the vessel via a small motor banca. Upon being discovered, one of the suspects displayed a firearm tucked at his waist and ordered the crew member to raise his hands. The crew, after being threatened, immediately fled to the bridge and reported the incident. Approximately 30 drums of 20L Paint, four pieces of copper screw from the cover of the Bosun Store and three copper fire hose nozzles were stolen. The VTMS Corregidor of Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) coordinated with CGSS North Harbor on the incident. Upon receiving the information, personnel of the substation immediately proceeded to CGSS Navotas to assist the IDU personnel conducting the investigation and communicating with the Master of the vessel.

Location: Approximately 5.3 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, a perpetrator with knife was sighted in the engine room workshop. The perpetrator attempted to threaten the engine room watchkeeping staff, who ran away and secured himself in the engine control room. The master was informed and the general alarm was activated. All crew mustered and a search was conducted, with no further sighting of the perpetrators. The crew members were not injured and nothing was stolen. No assistance was required and the vessel continued its voyage. The agent of vessel reported to Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA). Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was carried out to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN’s Maritime Security Task Force (MSTF) and SPCG were notified of the incident. Information was shared with the Indonesian authorities.

At Anchor While at anchor, the deck watchmen observed eight to ten perpetrators armed with long knives boarding the starboard aft deck. One of the perpetrators advanced aggressively, forcing the watchmen to retreat to the port quarter who then raised the alarm. The officer of the Watch (OOW) immediately notified the Master and crew. The ship attempted to contact the Bangladesh Navy and Port Control but with no response. The OOW then observed the perpetrators fleeing from the starboard quarter in two long wooden boats. A subsequent search confirmed no perpetrators remained onboard, but 2900 litres of assorted paint were stolen. The crew were not injured. The incident has been reported to local authorities as well as MPA (flag State).

At Anchor While at anchor, during a routine verification of hydro blower specifications for the enclosed-space equipment listing, the training Master was unable to locate the hydro blowers in the forecastle store. Subsequent checks with the crew confirmed that four hydro blowers, one pneumatic blower, one helicopter Rescue Equipment Box, and one coil of tiger rope were missing. The store lock was also found to have been broken. The crew were not injured and no assistance was required. A review of CCTV footage was inconclusive, as visibility was compromised by glare from the forecastle floodlight and forward tube lights. No intruders were captured on the recordings. The incident has been reported to the authorities by the local agent. The Superintendent of the ship also reported the incident to MPA (flag State).

A crew was slightly injured by the perpetrators with a minor laceration to his head, and the agent arranged for shore medical follow up. The incident was reported to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was carried out to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN and SPCG were notified of the incident. Information was shared with the Indonesian authority. The SPCG boarded the ship at Eastern Boarding Ground “B” (PEBGB) and conducted a search and investigation.

Location: Approximately 5.1 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, four perpetrators were sighted in the engine room. One of the perpetrators was armed with a long knife. The ship's general alarm was activated and crew mustered. After conducting a search onboard, master confirmed there was no further sighting of the perpetrators and some engine spares were stolen. All crew members were safe and accounted for. The incident was reported to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was carried out to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN and SPCG were notified of the incident. Information was shared with the Indonesian authority. The SPCG boarded the ship at Eastern Holding B Anchorage (AEHB) and conducted a search and investigation.

Location: Approximately 6.5 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, four perpetrators (not armed) were sighted at the starboard gangway. The ship's general alarm was activated and crew mustered. After conducting a search onboard, master confirmed there was no further sighting of the perpetrators and nothing was stolen. There was no confrontation between the perpetrators and crew; and all crew members were safe and accounted for. The incident was reported to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was carried out to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN and SPCG were notified of the incident. Information was shared with the Indonesian authority.

Location: Approximately 2.38 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, seven perpetrators armed with knives were sighted in the engine room. There was no confrontation with the crew. The master raised the general alarm and crew mustered. A search was carried out onboard with no further sightings of perpetrators. The crew were not injured. The incident was reported to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was carried out to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN and SPCG were notified of the incident. Information was shared with the Indonesian authority.

Location: Approximately 13.2 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, three unarmed perpetrators were sighted on board the ship. The master initiated a security search with no perpetrators found onboard. The crew were not injured. Nothing was stolen. The incident was reported to Singapore POCC. The SPCG boarded the ship at Eastern Bunkering B Anchorage (AEBB) and conducted a search and investigation.

Location: Approximately 3.2 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, five perpetrators boarded the ship. One of the perpetrators was armed with a knife. The ship’s general alarm was raised and crew mustered and accounted for. A search was carried out onboard with no further sightings of perpetrators. The crew were not injured. One crew’s mobile phone was stolen. The incident was reported to Safety Singapore VTIS. broadcast on anti-piracy watch was carried out to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN and SPCG were notified of the incident. Information was shared with the Indonesian authority.

Location: Manila International Container Terminal (MICT) Anchorage Area, Philippines
Description: At Anchor While at anchor, the duty crew noted that the cover of the hawse pipe of the starboard anchor was opened. After informing the 2nd officer, the general alarm, including the typhoon alarm was raised. A search was conducted with no perpetrators found on board. Subsequently, the master ordered an inventory and inspection of the deck equipment. The crew were not injured. Some ship property/stores were stolen. The incident was reported to VTMS Corregidor and CGS Manila. CGS Manila immediately directed the duty maritime patrol (MARPAT) team to verify the incident, and advised the Master to strengthen onboard security measures and increase roving duties to prevent similar incidents.

At Anchor While at anchor, a crew member was confronted by six perpetrators, reportedly armed with knives, at Bay 02 on the forward part of the ship. He was threatened, ordered to located remain silent, and confined in the bosun store beneath the forward mooring station. The crew member later freed himself and activated the fire alarm. The perpetrators briefly returned but were unable to gain entry, and subsequently escaped from the ship via the deck leading overboard. An immediate search of the vessel was conducted, with no perpetrators found onboard. Subsequent investigation by the ship’s crew revealed that the padlock and securing arrangement of the bosun store door had been tampered with, indicating forced entry. The stern access to the engineer’s passageway was also found to have been tampered with. A walkie-talkie and two hydrant caps were reported stolen. The company was notified, and the incident was reported to the local coast guard and customs authorities through the local agent.

Location: Vicinity Waters off Cavite City, Philippines
Description: At Anchor While at anchor, the crew noticed that several items, namely cable wires and parts of the ship's beam, were missing from the ship. The master subsequently confirmed that no other losses or damages were sustained, and that no further assistance was required. The crew were not injured. Upon receipt of the report, CGS Manila immediately directed CGSS Cavite City to conduct MARPAT operations and establish contact with the ship. Thereafter, all CGSS within the Cavite area were directed to conduct shore patrols and maintain heightened vigilance, particularly for possible sightings or recovery of the stolen items.

Location: Vicinity waters off Bauan, Batangas, Philippines
Description: At Anchor While at anchor, a seaborne patrol personnel of CGSS Bauan saw one of the perpetrators climbing the ship from an unnamed motor banca. The Philippine Coast Guard team immediately apprehended the perpetrator, and found a knife onboard the motor banca. A comprehensive search of the ship was conducted by the combined teams of CGSS Bauan and Special Operations Group Southern Tagalog. Three additional perpetrators were found onboard the ship, and all four perpetrators were turned over to the Investigation and Detection Unit - Southern Tagalog. Nothing was stolen.

Location: Approximately 6 nm off Pulau Nongsa (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, the master of the tug boat observed three sampans around the barge and three perpetrators on the barge taking scrap metals from the barge. About half an hour later, the perpetrators were sighted leaving in the sampans. The tug boat and barge continued their voyage and no assistance was required. All crew members were accounted for and without injury. Some scrap metals were stolen. The master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcasts on anti-piracy watch were initiated to remind all vessels to maintain vigilant watch at all times in the SS. RSN and SPCG were notified of the incident. Information of the incident was also shared with Indonesian Authority.

Location: Approximately 2.6 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, six perpetrators armed with knives were sighted at the steering gear room. The ship’s general alarm was raised. All crew members mustered and were accounted for. A search was carried out with no perpetrators found onboard. The crew members were not injured and some engine spares were stolen. The master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcasts on anti-piracy watch were initiated to remind all vessels to maintain vigilant watch at all times in the SS. RSN and SPCG were notified of the incident. SPCG boarded the vessel for security check at Singapore Anchorage but did not find any perpetrators on board. Information of the incident was also shared with Indonesian Authority.

Location: Batangas Anchorage, southeast of Brgy San Pedro, Bauan, Batangas, Philippines
Description: at anchor, several firefighting equipment and shipboard fittings were found missing from the open deck areas during a safety security round of the ship. It is believed that perpetrators boarded the ship during night time and stole the items. The incident was reported to the company, local agents, and VTMS Batangas. Additional security rounds were implemented, and all remaining bronze were removed from the open deck and secured on board as a preventive measure. CGS Batangas directed CGSS Bauan and CGSS Mabini to intensify seaborne patrols and conduct periodic radio announcements to all nearby ships in anchorage area to remain vigilant against illegal activities.

Location: Approximately 3.8 nm off Pulau Nongsa Beacon (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, the master of the tug boat observed one sampan alongside the barge with approximately five perpetrators sighted on the barge taking scrap metals. About 40 minutes later, the perpetrators were sighted left in the sampans. The tug boat and barge continued their voyage and no assistance was required. All crew members were accounted for and without injury. Some scrap metals were stolen. The master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcasts on anti-piracy watch were initiated to remind all vessels to maintain vigilance.

Location: Approximately 4.1 nm off Pulau Nongsa Beacon (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, approximately six perpetrators were sighted onboard the barge with three sampans alongside. At 1410 hrs, the master updated that the perpetrators escaped from the barge, and all three sampans departed from the area. Some scrap metals were reported stolen. The tug boat and barge continued their voyage and no assistance was required. All crew members were accounted for and without injury. The master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcasts on anti-piracy watch were initiated to remind all vessels to maintain vigilance.

At Anchor While at anchor, perpetrators from one motor banca boarded the ship and stole some cables. The incident was reported to PCG Substation Bauan. The PCG apprehended one perpetrator onboard the motor banca and conducted comprehensive search onboard and apprehended another four perpetrators. The perpetrators were charged under Violation of Article 122 of the revised Penal Code as Amended by R.A 7659- Piracy in General and Mutiny on the High Seas or in Philippine waters.

Location: In the eastbound lane of the Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS)
Description: While underway, nine perpetrators from three sampans were sighted alongside the barge removing scrap metals while the tug and barge were enroute from Singapore to Vietnam. After observing that all nine perpetrators had departed the barge, the master resumed the eastbound passage. At 1510 hrs, three sampans with nine perpetrators were again observed alongside barge taking scrap metals. At 1525 hrs, the three sampans departed from the barge. The crew was not injured. The master reported the incident to Singapore Vessel Traffic Information System (VTIS). Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was initiated to remind all vessels to maintain vigilance.

At Anchor While at anchor, the duty crew on routine rounds spotted ropes attached with hooks on the poop deck railings and immediately informed the bridge. Alarm was raised and crew mustered. Four perpetrators armed with knives were sighted escaping with stolen engine spares. The crew members were not injured. The incident was reported to port authority through local agent. PRC relayed the message to Indonesia Marine Police HQ.

Location: Approximately 2.66 nm from Pulau Ramunia (Malaysia), in the westbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, the master reported that two motorised small boats with five perpetrators onboard came alongside the barge. Four perpetrators were sighted stealing iron scrap from the barge. One of the small boats came alongside for a second time with three perpetrators and transferred scrap metals to the sampan. The master immediately mustered the crew and reported the incident to the shipping company and Singapore Police Coast Guard (PCG). Singapore PCG arrived at the spot and assisted by shadowing the barge. There was no confrontation with the perpetrators and no injuries to the crew. Some scrap metals were reported stolen.

Location: Approximately 5.4 nm from Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, the master reported that three perpetrators with batons were sighted in the engine room. The ship’s general alarm was activated and the crew mustered. A search was conducted with no perpetrators found onboard. All crew members were accounted for and without injury. Some engine spare parts were reported stolen. The master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was initiated to remind all vessels to maintain vigilance. The Republic of Singapore Navy’s (RSN) Maritime Security Task Force (MSTF) and Singapore PCG were notified of the incident. Information of the incident was shared with the Indonesian authorities. Upon arrival in Singapore, Singapore PCG boarded the vessel for security check with no perpetrators found.

Location: Approximately 2.74 nm from Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, the 2nd engineer sighted four perpetrators the steering gear room without armed with knives at confrontation. The ship alarm was raised and deck lighting was switched on. A search was conducted with no perpetrators found onboard. All crew members were accounted for and without injury. Some engine spare parts were stolen. The master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was initiated to warn all vessels to always maintain a vigilant watch in the Singapore Strait (SS). The RSN and Singapore PCG were notified of the incident. Singapore PCG boarded the vessel for security check at Singapore Anchorage with no sighting of perpetrators. Information of the incident was shared with the Indonesian authority.

Location: Approximately 4.8 nm from Batu Behanti beacon (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, two sampans were sighted alongside the towing barge and about 15 to 20 perpetrators were onboard the barge. The perpetrators then left the barge with some scrap metals. All crew members were accounted for with no injuries and no assistance required. The master immediately reported the incident to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was initiated to remind all vessels to maintain vigilance.

Location: Off Batu Berhanti (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While the tug boat towing barge was underway, the master reported to Singapore VTIS that a small boat with four to five perpetrators was alongside the barge and were removing the scrap metal on the barge. Over the next hour, several other small boats arrived and departed in phases, with a peak of seven boats engaged in In total, removing the scrap metal from the barge. approximately 45 perpetrators in 11 small boats were observed. Singapore VTIS was kept updated and crew safety was confirmed throughout. The company subsequently instructed the master to cross towards Singapore. The small boats later dispersed upon the approach of a Singapore PCG vessel. A small boat tried to return but escaped following the intervention of the Singapore PCG vessel. The tug boat and barge subsequently resumed their voyage to Vietnam. All crew members were accounted for, with no injuries reported. Safety broadcasts on anti-piracy watch were issued to remind all vessels to maintain vigilance.

Location: Approximately 1.8 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, two perpetrators armed with knives were sighted at the accommodation deck. The master raised the general alarm and mustered all crew. The perpetrators escaped upon being discovered. The master conducted a search and found no sighting of the perpetrators. All crew were accounted for and with no injury. Nothing was stolen. The master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS West. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was initiated to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN’s MSTF and Singapore PCG were notified of the incident. Information of the incident was shared with the Indonesian authorities. Upon arrival in Singapore, the PCG boarded the ship to conduct investigation. No sighting of perpetrators.

Location: Approximately 4 nm off Tanjung Sengkuang (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While the tug boat towing barge was underway, three perpetrators in four sampans came alongside and removed scrap metal from the towed barge. The crew was not injured, and no assistance was required. The tug boat and barge were en route from Singapore to Vietnam. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was initiated to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN’s MSTF and Singapore PCG were notified of the incident.

Location: Approximately 6 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, the crew discovered that the padlock leading to the engine room store was found broken. Some footprints were also sighted in the engine room. A search onboard was conducted, with no sighting of perpetrators. All crew members were accounted for, with no injury reported. Some engine spare parts and fire hydrant nozzles were stolen from the engine room store. The ship subsequently anchored at Eastern Bunkering Bravo and the master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was initiated to alert all mariners. The RSN’s MSTF and Singapore PCG were notified of the incident. Information of the incident was shared with the Indonesian authorities. Singapore PCG subsequently boarded the ship for security search, with no perpetrators found onboard.

Location: Approximately 2.4 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, two perpetrators armed with swords were sighted by ship crew in the engine room. Upon seeing the crew, the perpetrators immediately ran out to the poop deck and escaped. The master raised the general alarm and ship crew was mustered. A search onboard was conducted, with no further sighting of perpetrators. All crew members were accounted for, with no injury reported. Some auxiliary further engine spare parts were reported missing. No assistance was required. The master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was initiated to alert all mariners. The RSN’s MSTF and Singapore PCG were notified of the incident. Information of the incident was shared with the Indonesian authorities.

At Anchor While at anchor, the Officer of the Watch (OOW) was on the bridge conducting routine anchorage checks, when he sighted three unauthorised persons exiting the Bosun's store. The OOW raised the alarm and the crew was mustered, resulting in the perpetrators escaping. The perpetrators were dressed fully in black, one of them was wearing white gloves. They appear to be slim, athletic build and descended easily using rope to disembark from the ship. The crew conducted a search and it was discovered that the padlock of the Bosun's Store had been broken and the store accessed. Some of the ship’s stores were stolen. The crew was not injured.

Location: Approximately 7.3 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, two perpetrators armed with knives were sighted by the crew in the steering gear room. Upon seeing the crew, the perpetrators escaped immediately. The master raised the general alarm and the crew was mustered. A search onboard was conducted, with no perpetrators found onboard. All crew members were accounted for, with no injury reported. No further assistance was required. The master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS West. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was initiated to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN’s MSTF and Singapore PCG were notified of the incident. Information of the incident was shared with the Indonesian authorities. Singapore PCG subsequently boarded the ship for investigation and security search. Some engine spares were reported missing.

Location: Approximately 4.4 nm off Pulau Cula (Indonesia), in the eastbound lane of the TSS
Description: While underway, three perpetrators had tied up the oiler in the engine room, who witnessed that the perpetrators took some engine spares before they escaped. The oiler managed to free himself and notified the master. The master raised general alarm and mustered all crew. A search was conducted without finding any perpetrators. All crew were accounted for and safe. Some engine spares were stolen. The master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS West. Safety broadcast on anti-piracy watch was initiated to warn all vessels to maintain a vigilant watch at all times in the SS. The RSN and Singapore PCG were notified of the incident. Information of the incident was shared with the Indonesian authorities.

crew on patrol spotted two perpetrators near the forecastle area and reported to the bridge immediately. Upon being discovered, the perpetrators escaped from the ship. A subsequent inspection revealed that two fire hoses and two portable embarkation ladder lights were stolen. The crew was not injured. The master reported the incident to the Philippine VTIS. Description: While at berth, a crew member was patrolling the deck when he saw three perpetrators armed with knives emerging onto the deck. The crew member sounded the alarm immediately and notified the local authorities. Upon realising the crew was alerted, the perpetrators escaped immediately. A search was conducted onboard and two padlocks on the weather tight doors were found broken. Generator parts were stolen. The crew was not injured. It was later confirmed that another three perpetrators had also boarded the ship, and stole several pieces of timber lashing materials from the deck crane store. These were later recovered and returned to the ship by the authorities, who also arrested three of the perpetrators.
